record.trigger: A component receives two status-bearing range endpoints and owns both a failure flag and the corresponding plain-value outputs, with requirements saying any invalid endpoint raises failure, both valid endpoints clear failure, and no failure permits copying the range.
record.principle: Keep status classification and conditional range transfer together at their owning interface component. Preserve the distinction between trusting endpoint values and establishing numeric range constraints.
record.semantic_choice: Interpret 'any invalid' as disjunction, 'both valid' as conjunction, and 'if no failure then copy' as a one-way implication constraining both copied values. Do not infer output retention, default values, or numeric range validity when the antecedent is false.
record.structural_placement: Attach the detailed contract to the leaf interface thread that produces the failure flag and plain endpoints. Preserve the process wrappers and existing connections to the mode and alarm managers. Associate assumptions about input status production with the responsible input provider; assign relational environmental assumptions to the entity responsible for ensuring them.
record.repair_gate: Before accepting a proposed repair, require review of the original obligations and interfaces, proof of the status/transfer contract, and tests of every status combination. Reject repairs that suppress invalid inputs through new preconditions, weaken exact copying, impose unsupported failure-path output behavior, or change interfaces. If input status semantics or numeric assumptions are unresolved, leave application pending rather than inventing requirements.
prerequisites: The target has the same semantic ownership: one interface component produces a failure flag and two plain endpoints from two status-bearing inputs.
Valid and Invalid are mutually exclusive and exhaustive for this scoped instantiation; otherwise additional status behavior must already be specified.
Input values and statuses are sampled consistently for one component computation.
Endpoint input and output representations support exact copying without conversion or overflow.
The target's existing requirements and interfaces are available for preservation review.
exclusions: Inferring that Valid implies lower <= upper or any minimum range width.
Importing desired-temperature bounds or units from the thermostat context into the alarm range.
Specifying retained, zeroed, or otherwise fixed endpoint outputs during failure without a separate requirement.
Deriving system-wide freshness, scheduling latency, or alarm safety from this local transfer contract.
Adding new status variants or changing source interfaces.

parameters.name: lowerInput, upperInput
parameters.constraints: Each supplies a value and a binary Valid/Invalid status; preserve declared types, precision, units, and field mappings.

parameters.name: failure
parameters.constraints: Boolean flag; evaluated from the same sampled endpoint statuses as the transfer.

parameters.name: lowerOutput, upperOutput
parameters.constraints: Correspond to the respective input values without swapping or conversion.

dependencies: Existing status and endpoint type definitions.
Existing producer-to-consumer connections and requirement traceability.
preserved_obligations: Language: preserve any/both quantification and the direction of the no-failure implication.
Architecture: preserve every existing source port, type, direction, connection, process/thread boundary, dispatch period, and scheduling domain.
Contract: retain the invalid-status failure, valid-status nonfailure, and paired exact-copy obligations, together with all unrelated existing initialization and mode/status guarantees.
Implementation: compute failure from both sampled statuses and produce both exact endpoint values whenever failure is false; do not treat status validity as numeric validation.
Proof: establish the two status implications and conditional paired equality for every admitted input combination; establish that implementation sampling matches the contract interpretation.
Testing: exercise Valid/Valid, Valid/Invalid, Invalid/Valid, and Invalid/Invalid; check exact paired copying only when required, using distinct endpoint values to detect swapping.
Testing: include numeric boundary values supported by existing types and a reversed endpoint pair if admitted by the baseline assumptions, without inventing numeric validation behavior.
Repair: retain baseline guarantees and interfaces, repair the owning component locally, and repeat affected proof and tests before treating the repair as acceptable.

counterexample.scenario: The lower endpoint is Valid and the upper endpoint is Invalid. An implementation raises failure only when both endpoints are Invalid.
counterexample.expected_difference: The rule requires failure to be true because 'any invalid' is disjunctive. The faulty implementation clears failure. Under the required failure result, the conditional-copy clause alone does not prescribe endpoint output values.

record.notes: Observed: Manage_Monitor_Interface_i contains REQ_MMI_4, REQ_MMI_5, and REQ_MMI_6 with the status and conditional-copy structure described here. Its wrappers route endpoints to the alarm manager and failure to the mode manager. The supplied context discusses status-dependent behavior, assumption ownership, and locating detailed requirements within the functional architecture. Proposed: the implementation, proof, testing, and repair obligations are inferred application requirements, not observed completed work. The excerpt supplies no validation implementation or development results. Source references and hashes are reserved for assignment by the trusted controller.
source_english_patterns: If any alarm temperature status is Invalid then interface failure is True
If both alarm temperature statuses are Valid then interface failure is False
If no interface failure then copy alarm range
positive_paraphrases: Raise interface failure if either endpoint is invalid; clear it when both are valid.
Whenever interface failure is absent, output the respective lower and upper input values.
misleading_near_matches: Raise failure only if both endpoints are invalid.
When either endpoint is valid, copy the whole range.
If an endpoint is invalid, retain the previous range.
Valid endpoint statuses guarantee an ordered numeric range.

semantic_roles.actor: The interface leaf component that owns the failure flag and plain range outputs.
semantic_roles.condition: Either status is Invalid; both statuses are Valid; or the computed failure flag is false.
semantic_roles.effect: Assert failure, clear failure, or copy both corresponding endpoint values, respectively.
semantic_roles.modality: Required conditional guarantees within the scoped contract.
semantic_roles.quantification: Any means at least one of the two statuses; both means each of the two statuses; obligations apply to every admitted computation.
semantic_roles.temporal_scope: One component computation over consistently sampled inputs; no cross-component simultaneity is inferred.
semantic_roles.state_dependency: The scoped behavior needs no previous endpoint values; failure-path retention is unspecified by these clauses.
semantic_roles.units_and_boundaries: Preserve existing value representations and units. No numeric ordering, threshold, or width constraint follows from a Valid status alone.

record.formal_output_pattern: ABSTRACT contract on owning leaf component, for every admitted computation k: ((sL[k] = Invalid) OR (sU[k] = Invalid)) => failure[k]; ((sL[k] = Valid) AND (sU[k] = Valid)) => NOT failure[k]; NOT failure[k] => (lowerOutput[k] = lowerInput.value[k] AND upperOutput[k] = upperInput.value[k]). Represent the first two as input-guarded GUMBO compute cases; represent the third as an unconditional case whose guarantee is the implication. Under exhaustive binary status semantics, failure[k] iff either status is Invalid is derivable. No failure-path endpoint equation is added.
allowed_edit_scope: Owning leaf component's contract and implementation, subject to preservation of all baseline obligations.
Associated proof, test, and traceability artifacts.
Assumption documentation identifying responsible providers without silently strengthening the accepted environment.
required_baseline: Existing interfaces, architecture connections, scheduling declarations, and data definitions.
Existing component guarantees and initialization requirements.
Existing environmental assumptions and specified behavior for invalid inputs.
